title: Vertical restriction of a Segal space is an inner fibration
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, inner horns and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Reedy fibrancy of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and homotopy Segal spaces of [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence]. Let $W:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be Reedy fibrant and homotopy Segal. For any small simplicial set $T$ define a simplicial set $W/T$ by
$$(W/T)_p=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(T,W_p),$$
with its operators induced by those of $W$; this is an ordinary set of simplicial maps in each outer degree, not the vertical simplicial mapping space. Then $W/T$ is a quasicategory for every $T$. For every degreewise injective simplicial map $v:S\hookrightarrow T$, restriction $W/T\to W/S$ is an inner fibration: every commutative square with $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ on the left, $0<i<n$, has a diagonal filler. Neither completeness of $W$ nor a Kan condition on $S,T$ is assumed.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, Proposition 3.4 and Proposition 3.10, specializing the latter to W -> terminal; notation of Section 2. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this bisimplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Regard $W$ as a bisimplicial set and use the division objects of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. Thus $(U\backslash W)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(U\boxtimes\Delta^q,W)$ and $(W/T)_p=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(\Delta^p\boxtimes T,W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(T,W_p)$; the last bijection sends a natural transformation to its value at the identity $p$-simplex, with inverse given by restriction along each simplex of $\Delta^p$. For every monomorphism $a:A\hookrightarrow B$, vertical Reedy fibrancy gives a Kan fibration $a\backslash W:B\backslash W\to A\backslash W$. In particular $W_p$ is Kan (take $A=\varnothing$, $B=\Delta^p$), and both endpoint maps $W_1\to W_0$ are Kan fibrations (take either vertex inclusion).

source.place: Section 2, Proposition 2.5 and the division notation preceding Proposition 2.1; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: For $m\geq2$ let $I_m\subseteq\Delta^m$ be the union of the consecutive-edge subsimplices $[j,j+1]$, $0\leq j<m$. Let $P_m=W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$ have $m$ factors and let $H_m$ be the iterated path-model homotopy pullback in [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence]. The canonical constant-path map $P_m\to H_m$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Here are the hypotheses and induction: $P_1=H_1=W_1$; each $P_m=P_{m-1}\times_{W_0}W_1$ is Kan. Indeed, project a horn in $P_m$ to $P_{m-1}$ and fill it there; compose this filler with the last-target map to $W_0$. The given horn in the last $W_1$ factor lies over this base simplex, so the Kan fibration $s:W_1\to W_0$ supplies a compatible last-edge filler. The pair is a filler in $P_m$. The map from this strict pullback to the path pullback of $P_{m-1}\to W_0\leftarrow W_1$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. Replacing $P_{m-1}$ by $H_{m-1}$ in that path pullback is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]. The induction map commutes with the last endpoint, since both comparisons keep the last $W_1$ coordinate. Thus their composite is precisely $P_m\to H_m$. The homotopy Segal hypothesis makes $W_m\to H_m$ a weak equivalence; it factors as the strict consecutive-edge map $W_m\to P_m$ followed by $P_m\to H_m$. Two-out-of-three makes $W_m\to P_m$ a weak equivalence. Finally $I_m\backslash W=P_m$: maps from the union of consecutive edges are exactly compatible edge maps, degree by degree. Hence each spine restriction $W_m\to I_m\backslash W$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 3, Definition 3.1; expansion relating the item’s homotopy Segal convention to the strict Segal map; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A$ consist of the monomorphisms $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ for which $a\backslash W$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 1 says this restriction is always a Kan fibration. Consequently membership in $\mathcal A$ is equivalent to $a\backslash W$ being a trivial Kan fibration, hence to its lifting against every boundary inclusion. These implications use the Kan model structure and the model-category meaning of trivial fibration. For monomorphisms $u:A\hookrightarrow B$, $v:B\hookrightarrow C$, the restriction identity $(vu)\backslash W=(u\backslash W)\circ(v\backslash W)$ shows by two-out-of-three that $u,vu\in\mathcal A$ imply $v\in\mathcal A$. This is right cancellation among monomorphisms.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.4, class of monomorphisms inducing weak equivalences under left division; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: For $\delta_q:\partial\Delta^q\hookrightarrow\Delta^q$, Step 3 and the division lifting bijection give $a\in\mathcal A$ exactly when $a$ is monic and $a\pitchfork(W/\delta_q)$ for every $q\geq0$. Left lifting classes contain identities and are closed under pushouts, composition and arrow retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and under small continuous transfinite compositions by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. They are closed under small coproducts as well: restrict a lifting square to each summand, choose its filler and assemble the fillers by the coproduct universal property. Isomorphisms have the lifting property by using their inverse. Monomorphisms retain these closures degreewise: pushout identifies only the prescribed common subset, coproducts preserve injections, a continuous ordinal chain of injections embeds every stage into its union, and a retract of an injective function is injective. Intersections of classes having these closures retain them. Thus $\mathcal A$ has every saturation property of the spine-cancellation criterion used in Step 5, including the $q=0$ boundary test.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.4, saturation via Proposition 2.1 and boundary lifting; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: Step 2 puts every spine inclusion $I_m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq2$, in $\mathcal A$. Steps 3–4 verify right cancellation and saturation. Apply [lem-coef-spine-cancellation-inner-horns] to this class. Every inner horn $h:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ therefore lies in $\mathcal A$, so its restriction $h\backslash W:W_n\to\Lambda_i^n\backslash W$ is a trivial Kan fibration by Step 3.

source.place: Lemma 3.5 applied as in the proof of Proposition 3.4, implication (i) to (ii); read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: Fix $v:S\hookrightarrow T$ and a square with inner horn $h:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ on the left and $W/v:W/T\to W/S$ on the right. The division lifting bijection turns this into the square with $v$ on the left and $h\backslash W:W_n\to\Lambda_i^n\backslash W$ on the right: its horizontal maps are $S\to W_n$ and $T\to\Lambda_i^n\backslash W$. Step 5 makes the latter right arrow a trivial Kan fibration; the Kan model structure has monomorphisms as cofibrations, so it has a filler $T\to W_n$. Transpose this filler back. The result is a map $\Delta^n\to W/T$ extending the prescribed horn and restricting to the prescribed simplex of $W/S$. This proves the claimed inner-fibration property for every monomorphism $v$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.4, implication (ii) to (v); equivalently Proposition 3.10 with terminal target; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.

proof.text: Apply Step 6 to the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow T$. There is exactly one map from the empty simplicial set into each $W_p$, so $W/\varnothing$ is the terminal simplicial set. Each inner horn in $W/T$ fits into a unique square over this terminal object and hence has a filler. This is precisely the quasicategory condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The same argument with $S$ gives the asserted quasicategory for every $S$.

source.place: Corollary 3.6; read online, not archived. The expansion is agent-written.
